title: Logan would backstop Treasury trading while keeping monetary policy restrictive
summary: Lorie Logan favoured tighter monetary policy on 13 November and judged the Treasury market to be functioning well. She nevertheless argued that the Fed should prepare now for a breakdown in trading. In her view a well-designed liquidity backstop could give the FOMC greater freedom to keep rates where inflation required them. The difficult case arises when an intervention removes duration from the market for long enough to depress term premia. A tool deployed to restore trading could then ease financial conditions against the Committee’s inflation objective. These were Logan’s proposals and assessment of the economy. The speech recorded no FOMC decision.

For banks, readiness means knowing how much cash can actually reach a reserve account and at what time. Loan documents, pledged collateral, staff access and rehearsed procedures determine how much of a nominal facility is usable in a sudden outflow. The discount window was particularly relevant to smaller institutions with fewer market alternatives and larger banks seeking cash late in the day. Under primary credit, the lendable value of collateral sets the limit. Logan related how one bank successfully tested a large drawing late on a Friday. That demonstrated what the facility delivered for that borrower. It provides no distribution of settlement times across banks or collateral types.

Repo-active banks have another option. Standing repo operations lent against Treasuries and agency mortgage-backed securities to eligible counterparties at the same rate as primary credit. Logan counted 47 depository institutions among the counterparties. The New York desk had begun offering funding earlier, and the FOMC had removed the aggregate operation-size limit. Since 2024 banks had also gained an online discount-window portal. Changes to the Borrower-in-Custody programme simplified pledging loan collateral, and Reserve Banks were rehearsing collateral transfers with Federal Home Loan Banks. The latter matters when two funding sources depend on the same underlying pool of assets. The speed of release and transfer affects the amount available at the second lender.

Logan proposed three extensions. First, open the discount window on weekends and holidays. Instant-payment services already created overnight needs outside business days, and planned Sunday and weekday-holiday Fedwire operations in 2028 or 2029 could add to them. The Board of Governors would have to act. Second, prepare to centrally clear the Fed’s repo operations. A dealer that borrows from the Fed and lends the cash onward expands both sides of its balance sheet. Central clearing could permit netting, reduce the capital and balance-sheet cost and make it worth intermediating funds when risks are elevated. Covered private repos faced a mid-2027 clearing requirement. The central bank was exempt, and Logan favoured voluntary preparation because legal agreements and testing take time.

Third, she favoured advance documentation and collateral work with designated financial market utilities. There were eight such utilities. They retained primary responsibility for their liquidity. Under exceptional conditions the authorities might have only hours to prevent a shortfall at a clearing institution from spreading. Footnote 2 specifies the legal conditions: a majority of the Board must vote in favour, the Treasury Secretary must be consulted and the utility must show it cannot secure adequate bank credit. Logan’s claim about the benefit of a timely collateralised loan concerned that extreme scenario. The remarks grant no routine right to borrow.

The underlying Treasury-market vulnerability is that the asset investors sell to raise cash is also the asset dealers must absorb when everyone wants cash at once. Logan judged Treasury debt outstanding to have outgrown dealers’ capacity. In March 2020, market-functioning purchases also happened to support the desired monetary easing. That alignment could not be counted on when inflation was too high. March 2023 offered a different precedent: the Fed provided term funding for banks and raised its policy rate. A collateralised loan priced consistently with the target can address a funding shortage while the policy rate continues to restrain demand.

The binding constraint determines the instrument. A dealer with space to hold securities but insufficient cash can make use of a loan. When dealers cannot add assets, more borrowed cash alone may do little. Purchases can release balance-sheet capacity and give traders confidence there is a buyer. Logan suggested a separate account for market-functioning purchases and a commitment to sell the securities as soon as feasible. She expected the prospect of early resale to limit the term-premium effect relative to long-lived holdings. This was a proposal about the expected holding period, without a numerical estimate or a sale date.

For an investor judging the likelihood of intervention, Logan’s diagnostic is unusually specific. She would examine bid–ask spreads, market depth and the price impact of normal-size trades, allowing for the volatility prevailing at the time. Even a rapid rise in yields could reflect orderly price discovery. She thought trading had continued smoothly through substantial rate volatility and reserved intervention for extreme dysfunction. Communicating that distinction in advance could itself support participation. The speech offers a conditional guide to her own thinking and no yield level at which the Fed would buy.

questions.question: During stressed trading, is funding scarce or is dealer balance-sheet capacity exhausted?
questions.detail: Both can widen spreads, but they imply different demand for repos and outright purchases. Compare dealer inventories, repo rates and volumes, market depth and price impact after conditioning on rate volatility. Desk operations and Treasury market-functioning studies would help establish which constraint binds first.

questions.question: Would counterparties actually pass cheaper repo funding through to clients?
questions.detail: Logan identifies a legal route to netting, while the economic benefit depends on matched positions, clearing participation and binding capital constraints. Compare cleared and bilateral transactions around operating changes, using clearing-house rules, dealer balance sheets and Desk counterparty data to assess who would capture the saving.

questions.question: How quickly could market-functioning securities be sold without renewing the stress?
questions.detail: The separate-account proposal depends on a credible short holding period. The sale itself could absorb dealer capacity again. Examine the Desk’s operation-level purchase and runoff histories alongside execution costs and the distribution of holdings. The result matters for both the expected term-premium effect and the duration risk investors retain.

questions.question: How large is the weekend gap between payment obligations and usable collateral?
questions.detail: Payment hours are expanding faster than some borrowing arrangements. Compare timestamped weekend payment needs, collateral valuations and transfer windows with deposit-institution test-draw results. For clearing utilities, assess the additional legal decision time in footnote 2 before treating potential central-bank credit as available cash.
